scenes.tts: A thirsty mouse starts to drink. Within a minute, its thirst neurons go quiet. Yet its blood osmolality is still raised. What are they reading?
scenes.visual: A mouse at a water spout. Teaser, labelled schematic: the upper trace (thirst neurons, recorded continuously) drops at the first lick; below it, blood osmolality appears only as sample points, still raised at five minutes, with no line drawn between them. The question appears above.
scenes.narration: A thirsty mouse starts to drink. Within a minute, its thirst neurons go quiet. Yet its blood osmolality is still raised. What are they reading?

scenes.tts: Start with a loop. For water, the thing held steady is plasma osmolality, the concentration of dissolved particles in plasma.
scenes.visual: A loop diagram with three boxes: held steady, senses, pushes back. Box 1 fills: plasma osmolality, with small particles in a drop of plasma.
scenes.narration: Start with a loop. For water, the thing held steady is plasma osmolality, the concentration of dissolved particles in plasma.

scenes.tts: The S F O and O V L T sit in the front wall of the third ventricle. They sample the blood directly, where the blood-brain barrier is incomplete. A third site behind the barrier, the M N P O, integrates their signals.
scenes.visual: Box 2 fills: sensors. A sagittal brain sketch highlights the lamina terminalis. The subfornical organ (SFO) and organum vasculosum (OVLT) are drawn at a leaky barrier, open to the blood; the median preoptic nucleus (MnPO) is drawn separately behind an intact barrier, receiving arrows from both.
scenes.narration: The SFO and OVLT sit in the front wall of the third ventricle. They sample the blood directly, where the blood-brain barrier is incomplete. A third site behind the barrier, the MnPO, integrates their signals.
scenes.caption: The SFO and OVLT sit in the front wall of the third ventricle. They sample the blood directly, where the blood-brain barrier is incomplete. A third site behind the barrier, the MnPO, integrates their signals.

scenes.tts: Two effectors push back. Vasopressin saves water at the kidney. Thirst takes water in.
scenes.visual: Box 3 fills: vasopressin to the kidney; thirst to drinking.
scenes.narration: Two effectors push back. Vasopressin saves water at the kidney. Thirst takes water in.

scenes.tts: Both lower osmolality. The response opposes the error, so this is negative feedback.
scenes.visual: A minus sign appears on the return arrow from the effectors to osmolality. Label: negative feedback.
scenes.narration: Both lower osmolality. The response opposes the error, so this is negative feedback.

scenes.tts: Is there a separate comparator that judges the error? The comparison is spread across the sensing and integrating neurons. We summarize the result with a threshold and a gain.
scenes.visual: The question mark on the loop is replaced by a soft glow spread across the sensor and integrator boxes. Label: distributed comparison; system response described by threshold and gain.
scenes.narration: Is there a separate comparator that judges the error? The comparison is spread across the sensing and integrating neurons. We summarize the result with a threshold and a gain.

scenes.tts: Raise osmolality in a controlled way and record vasopressin. The plot is flat, then rises in a straight line.
scenes.visual: Axes: vasopressin up the side, plasma osmolality along the bottom. A line is drawn live: flat, a knee, then a straight rise. Numbers on screen: threshold 284 mOsm/kg, gain 0.43 pmol/L per mOsm/kg.
scenes.narration: Raise osmolality in a controlled way and record vasopressin. The plot is flat, then rises in a straight line.

scenes.tts: The knee is the threshold. It says when release starts. The slope is the gain. It says how much release grows.
scenes.visual: The knee is labelled threshold (when); the slope is labelled gain (how much).
scenes.narration: The knee is the threshold. It says when release starts. The slope is the gain. It says how much release grows.

scenes.tts: Suppose osmolality rises, but stays below threshold. Does vasopressin change?
scenes.visual: A cursor slides along the flat part of the line, left of the knee. A question mark appears.
scenes.narration: Suppose osmolality rises, but stays below threshold. Does vasopressin change?

scenes.tts: No. Below threshold there is no osmotic release. The line does not go negative.
scenes.visual: The flat part stays at zero. A dashed extension below zero is drawn, crossed out.
scenes.narration: No. Below threshold there is no osmotic release. The line does not go negative.

scenes.tts: Now two made-up people. Person P has the lower threshold. Person Q has the steeper gain.
scenes.visual: Two lines on the same axes: P (knee at 280, shallow slope) and Q (knee at 284, twice the slope).
scenes.narration: Now two made-up people. Person P has the lower threshold. Person Q has the steeper gain.

scenes.tts: Just above P's threshold, who releases more? And far above both thresholds?
scenes.visual: Two vertical markers on the axis, one just above 280, one well above 288. Question marks at each.
scenes.narration: Just above P's threshold, who releases more? And far above both thresholds?

scenes.tts: Just above P's threshold, P does. Q has not even started. Far above both, Q does. The steeper line wins.
scenes.visual: Just above 280 only P's line has risen. At 290 values appear: P 4.30, Q 5.16 pmol/L. The lines cross at 288 mOsm/kg, both at 3.44 pmol/L.
scenes.narration: Just above P's threshold, P does. Q has not even started. Far above both, Q does. The steeper line wins.

scenes.tts: So one number, a set point, cannot describe the loop. It takes at least two.
scenes.visual: The crossing point glows. A card: set point? Crossed out. Replaced by: threshold + gain.
scenes.narration: So one number, a set point, cannot describe the loop. It takes at least two.

scenes.tts: For osmotic vasopressin, the line is measured. Output is the gain, times how far osmolality is past threshold.
scenes.visual: Rule card builds: AVP = gain × max(osmolality − threshold, 0). Small label: osmotic vasopressin, healthy adults, illustrative. Below threshold, zero.
scenes.narration: For osmotic vasopressin, the line is measured. Output is the gain, times how far osmolality is past threshold.

scenes.tts: But water-balance circuits do not read the blood alone. Think of them as acting on an estimate. Feedback reads the blood. Feedforward adds what was just swallowed, or a learned cue.
scenes.visual: A second card: the estimate. Feedback reads the blood now; feedforward anticipates water already swallowed, or a learned cue.
scenes.narration: But water-balance circuits do not read the blood alone. Think of them as acting on an estimate. Feedback reads the blood. Feedforward adds what was just swallowed, or a learned cue.

scenes.tts: The hypothalamus acts through nerves, often in seconds. It also acts through hormones, whose effects usually build over minutes to hours.
scenes.visual: Two arrows leave the hypothalamus: wires (autonomic nerves, often seconds) and blood (pituitary hormones, usually minutes to hours).
scenes.narration: The hypothalamus acts through nerves, often in seconds. It also acts through hormones, whose effects usually build over minutes to hours.

scenes.tts: Threshold says when. Gain says how much. Keep the word estimate. The thirst neurons will show why.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: threshold = when; gain = how much; the estimate = the blood, corrected for what is on its way.
scenes.narration: Threshold says when. Gain says how much. Keep the word estimate. The thirst neurons will show why.
